newsitem.title: USA: WB Network says five affiliates defect from UPN.
newsitem.headline: WB Network says five affiliates defect from UPN.

text.p: The WB Television Network, owned by Time Warner Inc, Monday said five stations affiliated with rival United Paramount Network have agreed to switch to The WB in January, 1998.

The stations, owned or programmed by Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc, are WPTT-TV in Pittsburgh, WNUV-TV in Baltimore, WSTR-TV in Cincinnati, KRRT-TV in San Antonio and KOCB-TV in Oklahoma City. They will become primary affiliates of The WB for 10 years.

In a statement, Sinclair said The WB guaranteed Sinclair will receive compensation of $64 million for the first eight years. It could pay another $20 million over the final two years of the deal, but it has no obligation to do so.
Also, Sinclair's stations in Milwaukee, Birmingham and Tuscaloosa have extended their affiliations with The WB through January 2008. Glencairn owns the station in Milwaukee.
In addition, Sinclair's station in Greenville, South Carolina, WFBC-TV, will become an affiliate of The WB November 1999. WFBC-TV is owned by River City Broadcasting.
United Paramount Network (UPN) is owned by Viacom Inc and BHC Communications Inc, a 76-percent-owned unit of Chris-Craft Industries.
The WB and UPN launched their networks in late 1994 and early 1995, respectively, in an effort to form a fifth U.S. television network.
